Set up your term

Backpack keeps your classes, deadlines and notes in one place, and briefs you before each class on what you covered last time. Add your own courses to start — nothing is shared with anyone.

Notes search

All your courses. Pick one below, then type a name, year or term and the matching lines from your own notes show up as you type. Turn on AI search to get an answer worked out from your notes, with the lines it used.

Only use this during a test if the course outline or test instructions allow your own notes in digital form. Under Policy 71, the instructor decides which aids are allowed.

/ jump to the box · Esc clear · results update as you type
Missing something? Add your own line

Cram

Condensed sheets for each class: the must-know points, true/false traps, a flip deck, dates and who’s who. Pick a course, filter by module, or just type a keyword.

Take notes

Write however you want — fragments, half sentences, whatever comes out in class. Or drop a lecture deck on the page. When you’re done, pick a cleanup style below. Claude organises it without changing what you said, checks nothing was lost, then asks which class it belongs to. Select part of your notes first to clean up only that part.

Notebooks

Everything you’ve filed, kept together by class and in date order. Click an entry to read, edit or move it.

Study

Built strictly from your own filed notes, so a gap in your notes shows up as a gap here — which is the point.

Daily review

Thirty minutes on your own notes, every day. It picks what you are most likely to have lost: what you got wrong in quizzes, what you have not looked at in longest, and anything attached to a deadline this week.

30:00
Paused. The clock stops when you switch tabs or go two and a half minutes without touching anything — move the page to start it again.

✓

Done for today.

Ask

A study assistant that already knows your term — your timetable, every deadline, your marks and everything you’ve filed. Ask it what’s due, what a class covered, or to explain something from your own notes.

It reads your Backpack data each time you ask. It can’t see LEARN, your email or the web.

Grades

Type in a mark when you get one. This works out what fraction of each course has actually been graded and where you stand in the part that has — not a prediction of your final mark, just the arithmetic on what’s in so far.
